summary: Sunday's live start/sit show (Harmon, Josh, Boone, then Hayden) was chat-driven, and its most-discussed names were Jordan Mason, Omar Cooper Jr., Saquon, Emanuel Wilson and Puka. Graded against Sleeper at 6:28 PM, the clear hits were Omar Cooper (WR4), Tee Higgins "about to go crazy" (WR1), Pollard (RB1), Bucky vs CAR's missing corners (RB2), Braelon (RB10), Judkins (RB3), and Josh's Caleb Douglas over Ted Hurst (2 TDs vs zero). The misses were the flag plants for Woody Marks and Denzel Boston, Josh's McCarthy under-200 call (252), Boone's NYG-backfield fade (Skattebo RB6), Mason's dud and Addison. Kraft, Higbee, Gibbs/Goff, Waddle and Bo Nix are still live, with Emanuel Wilson, Saquon, Lemon, Pickens and Kelce to come. For Poncho, SUPERFLEX is the bright spot (137 to 97), while MAIN and DYNASTY need big SNF nights from Mahomes, Worthy and Kenneth Walker. And Caleb Douglas, the guy Josh picked, scored two TDs on three of your benches.

takeaways: Omar Cooper Jr. was the show's consensus darling and delivered (WR4, 5-115-1). Harmon's "better than anything Adonai Mitchell's done" film take looks right; he beat Keenan Allen, Malik Washington and KC in every question he was in.
Josh's best calls of the day were the quiet ones: Caleb Douglas over Ted Hurst (20.0 vs 0.0), Cooper over Keenan, Tee Higgins "about to go crazy" (WR1), and Tony Pollard "welcome to" (RB1, 3 TD).
The flag plants mostly flopped: Woody Marks (RB24, HOU lost in OT) and Denzel Boston (3-27) missed; Kraft is the one still alive.
Jordan Mason was the most-mentioned player and a dud (6.8, no catches). The "drive-by-drive" split read was right; the "big second half" read wasn't, because MIN never blew IND out (16-10).
Hayden's "attack cluster injuries" model: Bucky vs CAR's missing corners hit (RB2). The LAR-defense angle (Mayer, Jeanty) and the GB-LB angle (Goff/Gibbs) are not paying yet.
The fade-the-NYG-backfield call (Boone) missed badly: Skattebo 124 yards and a TD (RB6).
Higbee top-7 TE (Hayden) is at 0.4 with LAR up 28-6, a blowout that's killing LAR pass volume.
Things still to settle tonight and Monday: Emanuel Wilson (Josh vs Boone), Saquon RB7-9, Lemon, Pickens, Kelce "six catches", Goedert TE4.

title: FINAL Week 7 Start/Sit Cheat Sheet PART 2! LIVE Q&A + Actives/Inactives News | 2026 Fantasy Football
summary: The last pregame show was fast start/sit Q&A with Adam, Jamey and Jacob. The biggest fight was Adam's "sell Breece Hall before kickoff" call against Jacob and Jamey holding him (Jacob has him RB19 rest of season). Jacob's crazy take is that Ted Hurst is Tampa's best receiver today. Jordan Mason, Josh Jacobs ("normal workload") and Woody Marks were the most-asked players. Every live stat they cited checked out against Sleeper (Warren's 101 yards, Freiermuth's 2-20, the Saints' 7/6/5 rushers, Mooney's 109, Noel's 348 kick-return yards), except Egbuka's "25 targets." For you, the hosts backed Mason, Ollie Gordon, LaPorta and Braelon, and they'd have started Malik Willis, who is sitting on your Dynasty bench with 19.46.

takeaways: Breece Hall (your Dynasty bench, Out): the show split on selling. Jacob holds him RB19 ROS; Adam says sell now. The hosts agree running backs fetch the most in trades right now. If Braelon pops again today, Breece's price drops, so it's worth testing the market this week.
Braelon Allen: the hosts liked him over Saquon and Aaron Jones. He's at 12.7 PPR in progress.
Jordan Mason: the most-mentioned player and a near-consensus start; hosts want "15-20 touches," though one host prefers Dobbins.
Ollie Gordon II: started over Chase Brown, Dobbins and Judkins; the "61% of routes" every-down role note. Already 18.85.
Josh Jacobs report: "normal workload" (38:43), which matters for anyone facing Jacobs.
Waiver/trade radar for Week 8: Hockenson is a "next week" start vs DET; Micah McFadden for IDP; watch whether Omar Cooper's role shrinks in two-TE sets.
4:25 PM players still to play: Worthy and Mahomes (KC at SEA, low KC implied total and a Kelce ankle per the show), LaPorta (LaPorta over Likely), Amon-Ra, Bowers, Kenneth Walker.

summary: Sunday-morning lightning round with Adam, Dave and Heath before the 9:30 AM ET kickoff. The big news was Jacobs getting a "normal allotment" (Heath ~RB17), Puka expected but not certain, Skattebo back as the Giants' lead back with Tracy mixing in (avoid both), and Breece unlikely (now Out, so Braelon Allen is an RB2). Dave pushed Goedert as a must-start PPR TE, Darius Cooper and Michael Mayer as darts, and Vele (6+ targets every game), and Vele already has a TD in the early game. Heath leaned Higbee, Dobbins and the Seattle DST, and the closing pitch was to stream the Bengals DST for two weeks. Every stat I could check against Sleeper held up except Tre Tucker's "never stacks" numbers, which don't include his 2026 Week 2-3 follow-up (8.3 PPR).

title: LAST-MINUTE Week 7 Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advice! Actives/Inactives & Q&A (FFT Express)
summary: Adam and Heath ran a 9-minute pre-show at about 8 AM. The calls that hit were Braelon over the field with Breece out, Judkins as a top-20 back, Willis over Daniel Jones, Pollard over Corum, and Bam Knight over Allgeier. The misses were the Vikings backfield (Jones 3.6, Mason 6.8), Malik Washington's "11 points" (6.5), fading Omar Cooper (22.5), sitting Flowers for Chuba, and Tate over Kraft. For you, Braelon and Judkins delivered in Dynasty and SUPERFLEX, and Jacobs did in HEROES. Caleb Douglas (21.0) and Malik Willis (26.02) both sat on your benches.

takeaways: Heath's projections are low on Jacobs, and he's been wrong twice. Jacobs scored 20.1 on 11 carries because of his 5 catches. Don't bench Jacobs for Braelon-tier backs off this show.
Braelon Allen is a real RB2 while Breece is out (19.4, 17 carries, 7 targets). He's the waiver or trade story for Week 8.
Caleb Douglas (21.0) and Tre Tucker (21.3) beat every WR on Heath's waiver list. Douglas is the add to make in leagues where he's still free.
Daniel Jones is unplayable (4.62; Heath has him as the lowest-projected QB). Malik Willis (26.02) is startable while he's the Miami QB.
The Vikings backfield is a split that should be faded. Mason had 15 carries for 68 yards and Jones 8 for 26, against a matchup Adam called great.
MNF hedges: Saquon is still Questionable, so Pierce owners should be ready. Goedert is a top-10 TE with Wicks and DeVonta Smith out. Flournoy, Lemon and Darius Cooper are late-swap options.

title: Sal Vetri: "This News Changes Everything (Week 7)"
summary: Sal's Friday-evening injury roundup gets most of the big calls right on paper: Lamar, DeVonta and Wicks are all Out per Sleeper, Woody Marks is a must-start, and Saquon is a top-12 back against DAL's leaky run defense. Breece Hall is now Out, so Braelon Allen moves into Sal's RB14 scenario, and he's already in your Amon A Boat! lineup. In Taylor Snift, Worthy is a confident start, Mason is touchdown-or-bust, and Kendre Miller is already locked in Paris. Freddy's Saquon, Zay Flowers and Kelce all get good news here. Puka is still a game-time call for the late games.

segments.title: Cold open: 7+ hours on injury reports

Puka Nacua calf, game-time decision (hurt in Thursday practice, DNP Friday). Sal projects him IN. LAR pass-catcher fallout: Mumpfield WR36 if Puka out, more TEs (Higbee, Parkinson), Kyren's receiving role, Whittington ❓
Emeka Egbuka Out (concussion + foot). TB WRs with Baker back: Godwin WR31 (10.8), Ted Hurst 8.5 (Sal starting him in his 3WR/3-flex home league), Tez Johnson, Otton
Jeremiyah Love out again. Allgeier (RB27) vs Bam Knight (RB32); LaFleur quote: Allgeier on third downs, Knight early downs
Breece Hall practice arc (DNP Wed, LP Thu/Fri). Braelon's last 3 games without Breece: 88% snaps, 80% rush att, 64% routes, top-12 RB. Braelon RB14 if Breece out; ugly split if Breece plays
Saquon expected to play. PHI WR injuries (DeVonta, Wicks, Goedert knee), DAL run D allows most rush yds/g (149.8). Saquon 16 proj, top-12
Rashee Rice out again. Last week Worthy 27% TS, 7/7; Kelce 19% TS. Worthy WR26 (12.5), Kelce TE7 (11.7)
Montgomery out (groin), Jawhar Jordan IR → Woody Marks show (78% snaps, 61% rush att, 61% routes last week); ~16 proj, must start
DraftKings ad read
Tyler Warren out (reinjury), Pierce out. Last week Keenan Allen 32% TS (12 targets), Downs 18%. Allen WR28, Downs WR29; MIN "well-rested #1 defense"
Lamar Jackson high ankle sprain reveal. Sal: "I actually don't think Lamar Jackson is going to play"
Zay Flowers without Lamar: 33% TS last two games, leads NFL in yards per route run; still top-15
Judkins returns, Dylan Sampson activated off IR. Judkins RB21, 12.2 proj, TD-dependent
Broncos: Waddle chest/shoulder (limited, seen at practice), plays. ARI allows most yds/att (7.4) and 16 pass TDs in 6 games. "Bo Nix, please"
Charbonnet flip: expected to play "a lot," then ruled out mid-recording (Macdonald confirms). Emanuel Wilson 58% snaps last week; Holani more in 2nd half TNF; Sal wants nothing in SEA backfield
Subscribe ask (50%+ of viewers not subscribed)

Vikings healthy: Addison, Hockenson, Jefferson off the report; Mason full practices, questionable off IR; Sal prefers Aaron Jones; Ercolano stat: Mason ~6.7 pts/g with Jones active
Saints: Kamara LP all week (back). Miller last two weeks: 40% snaps, 57% rush att, 22 touches last week. Miller RB29 (8.9), Kamara RB30. Rather start Godwin; RB27-28s are "disgusting"
Dowdle knee, questionable, likely plays → Jaylen Warren RB12 in Paris
Breaking: Evans and Deebo ruled out (SF 6-0, Wk9 bye ahead). Kirk WR54, Cooks WR58, under 7 PPR; more Kittle, CMC, Kaelon Black
Outro; Sunday live stream 11 AM ET

bearish: Baker and TB passing game, SEA backfield, Judkins, Jordan Mason, NO backfield vs WRs, Kirk/Cooks, Keenan Allen/Downs (matchup), Mumpfield even if Puka sits.

summary: Hayden's Week 7 half-PPR WR board runs Puka, JSN, Amon-Ra, Chase, Lamb in the S tier, with GB @ DET called the game of the week (Watson WR6, Golden WR7). His biggest stands: Lamb way over Pickens (Quinyon Mitchell), Coker WR16 over consensus WR20, DeVonta Smith WR14 (now void because Smith is Out), and Michael Wilson as a buy-low that Josh openly doubts. Bold calls: Hayden says Shough throws a red-zone INT and Ja'Kobi Lane gets ~7 TDs this season. Josh says JJ McCarthy stays under 200 yards. Both pick Germie Bernard as the non-Love rookie to roster for the rest of the season. Most stats checked out against Sleeper. A few were a bit off: Jefferson had 79 yards (not 68) vs NO, Germie's W5 was WR21 (not WR9), Godwin's yards per catch is 9.0 (not 9.4), and Egbuka's targets per game are 8.2 (not 7.7). Since taping, Egbuka, DeVonta Smith and Lamar are all listed Out and Puka is Questionable. For you, Poncho: Coker is a start, Worthy has a low ceiling, and Amon-Ra is a buy-low start. In Super Flex, replace DeVonta Smith and Lamar. Freddy's Zay Flowers loses value with Lamar out, and Vele is his weak spot.

title: Sal Vetri: "My Week 7 Running Backs Rankings and Tiers"
summary: Sal's Thursday RB tiers (released Fri 10/23) put Gibbs, CMC, Bijan and Kenneth Walker in the S tier and Hubbard in the A tier on elite usage. He calls Woody Marks a must-start with Montgomery out, says Braelon Allen is RB12 because he expects Breece Hall to sit, wants Jacobs back in lineups right away, and keeps hammering the Jeanty sell. For you, Poncho, the key decision is in dynasty: if Breece is inactive, start Braelon. In MAIN, Taylor, Gordon and Mason are fine, and Kendre Miller is a desperation flex, but byes leave you few better options.

my_notes:
**MAIN LEAGUE (Myles High Club), your record 2-4**
- **Jonathan Taylor (starting):** Sal's RB8, brutal matchup @ MIN but "obvious starter." Keep him in.
- **Ollie Gordon II (starting):** Sal ~RB21, the "eat my words" guy at only +4 @ NYJ. Fine as an RB2.
- **Jordan Mason (starting, flex):** Sal had him RB33 on Thursday but said a full Friday practice would lift him to ~RB20. Sleeper shows no injury tag and projects him **9.6** (RB29 there). Playable.
- **Kendre Miller (starting, flex):** Sal RB26, "desperation flex," and says he'd rather start WRs over this tier. Sleeper projects **8.9**. Your bench WRs are **Keon Coleman (BUF bye), Stefon Diggs (WAS bye) and Caleb Douglas (MIA @ NYJ)**, so Douglas is the only healthy, playing alternative. With BUF, WAS and LAC on bye, Miller is probably your best option anyway. Your call, Poncho.
- **Omarion Hampton (bench):** LAC is on bye; not in Sal's ranks.
- **David Montgomery (bench):** Out per Sleeper. That's why Woody Marks (on BakedShady's team) is a must-start.
- Opponent-side notes: Freddy (FreddyB2) has **Bijan** (RB3) and **Saquon** (RB14, Questionable hamstring per Sleeper, MNF).

**DYNASTY (SCLSU Mud Dogs), your record 3-3**
- **Kenneth Walker III (starting):** Sal's RB4 despite the SNF revenge spot @ SEA and a KC team total of 20. Start.
- **Breece Hall (starting) vs Braelon Allen (bench):** This is the big one. Sal expects Breece **not** to play and has Braelon RB12 (16.1). Sleeper still says Breece **Questionable (quad)** and doesn't project him in its top 50 RBs, while Braelon projects **15.4**. If Breece is inactive at ~11:30 AM ET, swap Braelon in. NYJ hosts MIA at 1 PM.
- **Rico Dowdle (bench):** Sal RB34, only a play if PIT stays close. Leave him on the bench.
- **Justice Hill (bench):** Sal ~RB38-41. Bench.
- **Isiah Pacheco (bench):** IR; Sal doubts he returns this year.
- Any lineup changes need your OK, Poncho; nothing has been changed.

Brown's speed, Tanner McKee and Waddle, and up on Jacobs (about 15 touches), Bryce Young, Purdy as QB6, and Jaylin Noel as the top replacement WR. The hosts liked CAR, SF and DEN as streaming defenses over your beat-up Rams. Freddy's MAIN lineup starts a questionable Saquon, and his dynasty roster lines up well with this show's calls (Noel, Bernard, Mumpfield if Puka sits).

title: 9 League-Winning Players to carry you into Fantasy Football playoffs
hosts: solo. Usual co-host Ryan Heath was out (Jacob says he was sick earlier in the week
missed the recording slot; Heath "back next week").
summary: A Jacob Gibbs solo trade-target show. His nine-ish league winners are Parker Washington, Jordan Mason, the cheap Dolphins (Ollie Gordon, Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell), Jeremiyah Love, Ashton Jeanty, Bhayshul Tuten (his loudest call, RB1 the rest of the way), Drake London, Zay Flowers and Tucker Kraft. For you: in MAIN you already own Mason, Gordon and Douglas, and Chris Bell is sitting on waivers. In DYNASTY, hold Douglas, and musicm45 owns Bell, Tuten and Washington if you want to shop.

segments.title: Intro: solo show, Ryan Heath out; "no parameters, no rules," so Drake London is allowed
#1 Parker Washington (JAX): bye-week buy, schedule, Jaguars offense metrics
Cheap version: Jakobi Meyers; "you want at least one Jaguar"; trade ideas (Golden, Olave, Watson for Washington)
Jacob's ROS WR board: Washington WR10
#2 Jordan Mason (MIN): outside-zone scheme, rush success rate, YAC, schedule; ROS RB21
#3-5 cheap Dolphins: Ollie Gordon II, Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell
Caleb Douglas film notes and separation data; Chris Bell as an "A.J. Brown" comp
Break
#6 Jeremiyah Love (ARI): injury, FantasyPros consensus drop, Cardinals offense stats
#7 Ashton Jeanty (LV): efficiency slump, Raiders non-QB production, late schedule
#8 Bhayshul Tuten (JAX): ROS RB11, role growth, route rate spike
Break
#9 Drake London (ATL): WR7 ROS, trade packages, CeeDee Lamb as a sell-high idea
London with Penix splits; Zay Flowers (BAL) split and WR6 ROS
Tucker Kraft (GB): last buy window, two-year TE profile
Wrap: slow starts off injuries should have been expected (Kraft, Jeanty, Love, Tuten); Zay and London have injury/QB discounts

disagreements.Elsewhere: Thursday (SS7) both BTBS hosts said "Oh yes" to Odunze + Mason for Tuten

disagreements.Jacob here: RB19, possible single digits vs LAR

disagreements.Elsewhere: Dan Schneier on Thursday: "I'm out on that" at TE6

disagreements.Jacob here: Sell for Kraft plus (NYG QB worry)
disagreements.Elsewhere: Dan on Thursday: TE5, keep riding

takeaways: Tuten is Jacob's top buy (ROS RB11, says RB1 the rest of the way). His bye is now (JAX Week 7), the classic buy window. Week 8 vs IND is flagged as a breakout spot.
Parker Washington is a bye-week buy too (ROS WR10). Offer Golden-, Olave-, or Watson-type WRs who've scored more.
Zay Flowers (WR6) and Drake London (WR7) are "shouldn't be gettable but might be." Lamb is a sell-within-a-month idea before his rough Weeks 12-16.
Kraft before Sunday: the soft DET matchup could close the window.
Love and Jeanty are patience buys for contenders with depth. Jeanty may be cheaper after another dud this week.
Cheap/waiver darts: Chris Bell, Caleb Douglas, Jakobi Meyers, Chris Rodriguez (Tuten insurance).
Mason (ROS RB21) has the easiest playoff path: DET, WAS, NYJ in Weeks 15-17.

title: Here's What I'd Do with the 10 Most Confusing Players Right Now
summary: On Friday morning the BDGE rankings host (very likely Nick Ercolano, based on the video description) went through fantasycalc's 10 most-traded players. His buys are Josh Jacobs, Michael Wilson and Egbuka (as a buy-low), plus Coker if anyone's down on him. He's holding Ollie Gordon and Chase Brown (leaning buy). His sells are Saquon ("as clear as day"), Hampton and Pickens (hold/sell), and A.J. Brown is now sell/hold after a second TNF dud, a day after Thursday's rankings had him as Feels Good. Every box-score number he gave checked out against Sleeper. For Poncho, that means keep starting Gordon and Coker on Taylor Snift and sell Hampton for anything. Freddy is starting Saquon against Taylor Snift today.

segments.title: Intro: buy/sell/hold on the 10 most-traded players from fantasycalc
1. Ollie Gordon II (MIA RB): HOLD
2. Chase Brown (CIN RB): HOLD, "much closer to a buy"
3. Saquon Barkley (PHI RB): SELL ("as clear as day")
4. A.J. Brown (NE WR): SELL/HOLD ("definitely not a buy")
Arena Club slab-pack rip (Drake Maye blue/orange shock /35, gem mint 10) + promo
5. Michael Wilson (ARI WR): BUY
6. George Pickens (DAL WR): HOLD/SELL
7. Josh Jacobs (GB RB): BUY ("very much a buy")
8. Jalen Coker (CAR WR): HOLD, buy if anyone's down on him
9. Emeka Egbuka (TB WR): BUY LOW
10. Omarion Hampton (LAC RB): SELL ("no chance I'm buying")
Recap of the 10, "once a month" trade video, BDGE Off Center pack-ripping channel, Sunday Twitch stream

disagreements.text: A.J. Brown: Thursday's WR rankings (BDGE-4) had him Feels Good; after the TNF dud he's now sell/hold. That's a real step back from 24 hours earlier, and he says so ("I was kind of unsure").
Josh Jacobs: consistent with BDGE-3 ("right back into the role"), and that's still the open H2H-1024-8 row against Jamey Eisenberg's sell-high.
Michael Wilson: consistent with BDGE-4 (start Wilson over Waddle).
*Mine:* Chase Brown "closer to a buy" goes against the market (he's on the most-traded list because people are selling).

predictions.prediction: Josh Jacobs is a bell cow, 20+ touches a game, with all the goal-line work (17:10).
Samaje Perine does not out-snap Chase Brown going forward (4:42).
Michael Wilson becomes ARI's top WR again; "great wide receiver two" ROS (14:08).
Egbuka has a good second half as a borderline WR2/3 (20:32).
Saquon is a sell; his value drops if he flops on MNF vs DAL (5:23).
Ollie Gordon gets 15+ touches in good matchups, about 11–13 points a week (2:41).
Hampton doesn't get a 70% touch share; the split stays (21:53).
A.J. Brown is not his 2023–24 self (9:04).

takeaways: Jacobs is the buy of the list. In MAIN he's on Amon Raw, Next Question's *bench* right now; that's a manager who might sell. In DYNASTY he starts for Texas Rattlesnake.
Sell Saquon before MNF if you can. He's Questionable (hamstring) and plays Monday. Freddy is starting him against Taylor Snift today.
Hold Ollie Gordon and Coker (both on Taylor Snift). Neither gets you fair value in a trade.

title: Sal Vetri: "5 Players You Need to Trade Away Before It's Too Late" (Week 7 sell-highs)
summary: Sal's sell list is five main names (Jeanty, Metcalf, RJ Harvey, Egbuka, Worthy) plus quick spike-sells (Tucker, Pitts, Corum, Omar Cooper Jr.), all under one rule: sell only for real value. title: Sal Vetri: "Answering Your Week 7 Fantasy Football Questions" (Thursday live Q&A)
summary: Sal's Thursday pre-TNF Q&A was an hour of trade and start-sit triage. His biggest moment was the live Puka calf scare. He said Puka probably sits, and Puka played and scored. His best calls were Burden, Rhamondre over Mason, Woody and Ollie over Mason, fading Kirk, Skattebo's role returning, Zay Flowers and Tee Higgins. His misses were Likely over Loveland, Nico over Bernard, the Omar Cooper fades, Roschon, and Woody over Bucky. For you, the takeaways are to fade Jordan Mason (MAIN, SUPERFLEX), hold Hampton through the bye, treat Braelon as a short-term starter until Breece is back (DYNASTY, SUPERFLEX), and keep Walker and Amon-Ra off the trade block. On Freddy's side, Sal would sell his DK and Jameson Williams and is all-in on his Zay Flowers and Gibbs.

title: Week 7 Start Sit Advice (Part 1) | MUST-Start Players & Big Names to AVOID | 2026 Fantasy Football
hosts: Heath Cummings. Dave Richard was off (his rankings are quoted).
summary: Thursday's Part 1 start/sit show (Adam, Jamey, Heath) covered the seven AFC home games. **Jamey's loves:** Braelon Allen (start of the week if Breece sits), Kyler Murray, Metcalf and Germie Bernard. **Heath's above-consensus picks:** Roschon Johnson (busted on TNF, under 2 points), Kirk Cousins as a top-12 QB, and Pat Freiermuth on National Tight Ends Day. **Avoids:** Mahomes (both, hard), Michael Wilson, the Saints RBs, Charbonnet, Keenan Allen and Loveland. Heath's Loveland fade lost: 19.9 on TNF. Most of the stats checked out against Sleeper (Kamara/Miller touches, Bernard's 21 targets, Flowers' Huntley games, Mayer, Washington, Watson), with a few misses (Rodgers' "four straight 20+," Concepcion's floor). For you, Poncho: in DYNASTY, **if Breece Hall is ruled out, start Braelon Allen**, the hosts' start of the week. In MAIN, you're stuck with Mahomes at QB with Josh Allen on bye, Kendre Miller is the starter the hosts like least (Hampton is on your bench), and the Jets DST is the hosts' preferred stream over your Rams. Freddy's MAIN lineup is mostly players the hosts like (Rodgers, Metcalf, Flowers), and Barkley is "expected to play."

takeaways: If Breece Hall sits, Braelon Allen is a must-start (Jamey's start of the week; Hall didn't practice Wed; Sleeper lists Hall Questionable). Both hosts take Braelon over Chase Brown if Hall is out.
Get away from Mahomes if you have a real alternative: Gino, Kyler, Rodgers, Stafford, Stroud, Purdy all ranked over him by at least one host. Rashee Rice is Out per Sleeper.
Start both Steelers WRs (Metcalf slightly ahead of Bernard), and Jaylen Warren as a borderline RB1. Rodgers is a usable QB12.
Fade Shough, the Saints RBs, Michael Wilson (if Surtain plays), Keenan Allen vs MIN, and the Giants RBs.
Woody Marks is an RB2 with a 20-carry path; Zay Flowers is a must start (Heath's top 15).
Chase Brown is a start by default, but watch his workload split with Perine. Perine is the better stash than Roschon now that Monangai is expected back.
Charbonnet: both hosts lean him over Emanuel Wilson as a flex for the TD equity, but Sleeper still shows him Out (ACL/PUP tag). Check before lock.
TE: Kelce is a low-end TE1; Freiermuth a low-end starter (Heath's sleeper); Higbee over Mayer over Parkinson.
Streaming D: Jets (vs MIA) and Bengals (if Huntley starts) over the Rams; avoid the Steelers DST.
Waiver: Christian Kirk (Evans not expected, Deebo missed) and Fernando Mendoza in Superflex.

title: Week 7 Rankings I Start/Sit I Fantasy Football Advice
summary: Thursday's BTBS start/sit show was Jacob's full Week 7 rankings plus chat Q&A. Both hosts were all-in on Jordan Mason, endorsed Aaron Rodgers hard, and made Braelon Allen's value hinge on Breece Hall. The Thursday results went their way on Swift, Stevenson, Loveland, Burden and Maye, while the Pop Douglas hype (5.3 PPR) and AJ Brown (7.8) missed. For you: Mason is a start in MAIN, Kendre Miller is shaky but your bench is thin, and in DYNASTY you should check Breece Hall's status before 1 PM and pivot to Braelon if he's out. Hockenson is active and endorsed.

segments.title: Intro: Thursday = listener-question show; BTBS Sicko dynasty league trade talk ("insulting offer = no counter")
TNF preview: Caleb vs Drake Maye, Patriots O-line worries, Vegas (CHI 4th-highest implied total, NE 14th)
RB rankings (Swift RB8 & the Roschon usage correction; JT RB10; Saquon/Pierce; Breece/Braelon; Mason vs Aaron Jones; Jeanty; NE/DEN/ARI backs; mixed backfields; Seattle/Charbonnet; Henderson)
Break
WR rankings (CeeDee Lamb vs Fangio, Golden WR7, Nabers slot rate, Coker vs T-Mac flip, AJ Brown, Pickens, Mingo, PIT WRs, Pop Douglas separation, Keenan vs Downs, Evans/SF flyers)
Break
TE rankings (Kittle w/o Evans, LaPorta, Likely TE5, Kraft "out on that", Hockenson, National Tight End Day, Freiermuth birthday)
QB rankings (Purdy QB1, Lamar QB2?, Maye over Caleb, Stroud, Kyler QB10, Shough, Rodgers' game log, Bo Nix QB15, McCarthy)
Chat Q&A: start/sit, flex calls, trades (Likely trade-tier ladder, Odunze + Mason for Tuten)
Outro

disagreements.Jacob: Prefers Pierce/Rhamondre/Aaron Jones over a hamstring Saquon

Burden 23.7 already banked; Mason pending Sunday

disagreements.Dan: Lamb and Pickens both fine vs Fangio

takeaways: Jordan Mason is both hosts' favorite RB start of the week (RB17, IND at home, MIN -6.5). Healthy per Sleeper now.
Breece Hall decides Braelon Allen: RB12 if Breece sits, ~RB20 for both if he plays. Breece is Questionable (quad) per Sleeper.
Start Aaron Rodgers over Shough/Nix/Cousins; QB8, QB3, QB12, QB13 the last four weeks, PIT -3 vs NO (9:30 AM ET kickoff, ESPN line).
Hockenson is a "Hock it up" start vs IND (Dan).
Keenan Allen is only WR41; he's a full-PPR floor play ("six for 38"), not a ceiling play.

title: BDGE: "Ranking Every Week 7 Wide Receiver as a Sit or Start" (Week 7 WR tiers)
summary: BDGE's Thursday Week 7 WR rankings (same unnamed solo host as Wednesday's RB video, 32:50) put every WR into five tiers. TNF went half his way: Luther Burden (23.7 PPR) and the low-floor Pop Douglas (5.3) and Kalif Raymond (0) calls hit, but his Feels Good A.J. Brown laid a 7.8 and NE's targets spread out instead of condensing. Both of his injury reads are now Sleeper "Out" tags (Egbuka, Rashee Rice). His Sunday calls to watch are CeeDee going "nuts," the Metcalf/Bernard target share, Carnell Tate and Denzel Boston as strong dub flexes, Michael Wilson over Waddle, and Adonai Mitchell over Omar Cooper. For Poncho, Coker (Feels Good) and Amon-Ra (Must Start) look good. The flags are Worthy in MAIN (only a shaky flex even with Rice out) and Shaheed in DYNASTY ("rather not shaky flex"), and neither has an obvious bench upgrade. Freddy is starting Mumpfield ("floor is a zero") and a Lamar-less Zay Flowers.

Young CLE/TEN receivers over the vets: Carnell Tate and Denzel Boston are dub flexes, and Jeudy/Ridley are Rather Nots.

title: Week 7 Fantasy Football RB Rankings (Top 40)
url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p-kuqEsFEaM · Runtime: 50:50 · Sponsors: Farmers Insurance (open + read in the Swift segment), DraftKings ("Stand your ground" pick at the Woody Marks reveal; promo read before Roschon Johnson)
summary: Hayden's Week 7 half-PPR RB top 40 starts Gibbs, CMC, Bijan, Henry, Walker. His biggest stands are Woody Marks at RB10 (consensus RB19, "fringe RB1" with Montgomery out), Swift at RB7, and a late drop of Jonathan Taylor to RB12 at Minnesota, the toughest RB matchup in the league. TNF already graded several calls. Swift (19.0 PPR), Luther Burden (23.7), Loveland (19.9) and Rhamondre (22.5) all hit. His live swap of Roschon Johnson over Pollard missed (1.3 points). The stats they cited mostly passed the Sleeper check, but a few were slightly off: Chuba was RB13 once in half-PPR, Swift's no-Monangai run was RB8, and Pierce was RB14 last week. For you, Poncho: JT is still a start but with lower expectations. In DYNASTY, Hayden expects Breece to sit and ranks Braelon RB11, so swap him in if Breece is ruled out. Jordan Mason off IR is the riskiest of your MAIN flexes.

Hayden Winks.text:
- **Stance:** Ranks by Vegas team total plus usage, with a matchup tilt. Above consensus on Woody Marks (+9), Swift (+3) and Braelon. Below consensus on Jonathan Taylor (RB12 vs RB7). Bearish on Jeanty's efficiency, Allgeier, Pollard and the Giants/Seahawks backfields.

title: Sal Vetri: "7 Players About to GO NUCLEAR in Fantasy (Trade For Them Now)" (Week 7 buy-lows)
summary:
Sal's Week 7 buy-low list has eight names. **DJ Moore** is his favorite buy at any position (33% target share in two healthy games, back from the bye in Wk8), and **Chase Brown** is next (the fumble cost him Wk5, but CIN's offense is top 10). He also wants **Jaylen Warren** (74% snaps with Dowdle back, a top-15 RB ROS), **Woody Marks** as the cheap one (78% snaps, Montgomery out), and **Zay Flowers** and **Christian Watson** if a losing team will panic. **Ladd McConkey** ("it feels gross") is a stash-buy, and **A.J. Brown** is a "significant buy low" who then went 3/48 on TNF. For Poncho, nothing forces a lineup change before Sunday. The best angles are trades: A.J. Brown from 0-6 cdurka55 in DYNASTY, and DJ Moore or Chase Brown from motownmatt in MAIN.

---
*Queue: Sal also posted RWMuTkTZGqQ "5 Players You Need to Trade Away Before It's Too Late," 7y6AFsWTrOw "My Week 7 Running Backs Rankings and Tiers," and hA_6llL2d40 "This News Changes Everything (Week 7)" (Sat 10/24). They're next, one per run.*

segments.title: Cold open: buy-lows "before week seven begins and… before your league mates do"

DJ Moore: shoulder (AC joint), 2 missed games, bye; 17% season target share is skewed; healthy-game splits via Loveless (38% and 30%); Bills #1 in PPG, #3 in yards; ROS 53rd → top 50; would swap Jameson Williams or Michael Wilson for him
Zay Flowers: 35% target share with Tyler Huntley; game-log walk; Ryan Heath stat (33% TS, 44% of yards, above JSN's 2025); ROS 16th, maybe above Derrick Henry and Chris Olave

Jaylen Warren vs Rico Dowdle: Dowdle 7/40 back from toe; Warren 74% snaps, 63% rush attempts, 46% routes; 163 total yds and 22 PPG over 3 weeks; 7.2 yds/touch leads NFL; ROS 27th / RB11; Blueprint plug; "very concerned about Gentry [Jeanty?]"
DraftKings ad (promo code SAL)
Woody Marks: London vs JAX; 15/56 (season high vs JAX RBs); Jawhar Jordan's 25-yd TD is noise; 78% snaps, 61% rush share, 61% routes; Stroud and Nico Collins rolling
Christian Watson: SNF 3/64 while Golden went 6/100/TD; two unlucky plays; game log; Jordan Love in the MVP mix; GB pass-pro jump (31st → 1st in pressure rate allowed); ROS 21st
Subscribe ask ("over 60%… are not subscribed")
Chase Brown: out-carried by Perine after a fumble, RB21 in PPG, last year's RB34 → RB6 arc, CIN top-10 PPG and 343 yds/game
Free start/sit tool demo (fantasyfootballstarts.com): Warren 12.3 vs Chase Brown 11.9
Ladd McConkey: concussion, Wk7 bye; Dr. Chona's "most players return within two weeks"; injury-by-injury log; WR13/WR12 rookie splits; McDaniel play-calling rumor; booger incident (≈17:05)
A.J. Brown quick hit: 97% routes, team-high 10 targets, Doubs hurt
Outro, plug for his panics video

title: Buy Low & Sell High Trade Targets Ahead of Week 7  | 2026 Fantasy Football Advice
hosts: Jamey Eisenberg (joined ~3:10). Dave Richard was off ("Dave won't be here today").
summary: A Wednesday buy-low/sell-high show with Adam, Heath and Jamey. **Buy:** Bucky Irving (Heath) and DJ Moore (Jamey), plus Drake London, McConkey and A.J. Brown. **Sell:** DeVonta Smith (Heath) and Josh Jacobs (Jamey); the hosts' own team flipped Jacobs for Saquon Barkley on air. **Hold:** the Packers WRs and Bowers. Adam's Likely and Giants-QB stats checked out perfectly against Sleeper (TE1, 9.8 targets a game, 5 TD; Giants QBs 324 yds/g, 8 TD, 5 INT, 43.3 att over three games). The TNF calls mostly hit: Maye, Caleb, Henry, Burden, Loveland and Swift did, while A.J. Brown, Douglas and Heath's Roschon pick didn't, and Jamey beat Heath on Rhamondre (22.5). For you, Poncho: in MAIN, Coker is a start and LaPorta is the TE1 you'd want, Freddy's Barkley is the injury to watch, and both hosts preferred Caleb to Freddy's Rodgers. In DYNASTY, the hosts like your bench back Braelon Allen over Breece, Bowers is a hold, and you should re-check Hockenson. Freddy left 34 TE points (Loveland 19.9 and Henry 14.1) on his dynasty bench Thursday.

- **Bullish:** DJ Moore buy low ("an easy one to go get for me"), Packers WRs (hold unless superstar return), Drake Maye ("top three quarterback this week"), Hunter Henry ("for me, he's a top 10 guy this week"), Rhamondre Stevenson ("I still view him as the lead running back"), McConkey buy low (attr. likely), Brock Bowers (only sell for 2-3 top-15 starters).
- **Bearish:** Josh Jacobs (sell high), Brian Thomas Jr. ("he's droppable"), "get what you can for Pickens" thinking, Romeo Doubs ("zero expectations," attr. likely).
- **Quotes:** "If you could trade him now for something of significance, I would do it before maybe he doesn't look so good in this first game." (Jacobs) · "This is a throwback offense essentially." (GB) · "Jacobs for Price, Wilson, and Barkley? … I think you have to do it."

takeaways: TNF is done, so this is for ROS: Burden (23.7), Loveland (19.9) and Rhamondre (22.5) all hit. The two calls that missed were Heath's Roschon pick and A.J. Brown as a WR2.
Buy Bucky Irving before Baker returns. Heath's case is targets (7 in Wk1, then 3-4 a game), not rushing efficiency.
Sell DeVonta Smith if someone pays for the 14-target game, but note Adam's point: his schedule through Wk14 is soft.
Sell Josh Jacobs on name value before his first game back (Jamey); the hosts' own team flipped him for Barkley.
Don't sell the Packers WRs (Watson WR3 overall, Golden WR14 per game, both verified) unless you get a stud back.
Bowers is only for sale for two or three top-15 starters.
Drake London is a buy if his manager is frustrated by 0 TDs (10/6/11/10 targets with Penix verified).
BTJ is droppable unless traded (30-35% odds per the hosts).
Likely is a reasonable sell if you can get a steady TE plus a piece; Heath expects a 10-20% fade as the schedule hardens (HOU, bye, PHI).
Michael Wilson: zero-for-eight on end-zone targets; bench him if Surtain plays.
my_notes:
**MAIN: Taylor Snift (Poncho), 2-4, vs Freddy's "Flowers for Ms. Jackson" (2-4) in Week 7**

**Freddy (your MAIN opponent):** He starts **Saquon Barkley**, whom the hosts just traded *for* ("sounds like Barkley's getting close to return"). Check Barkley's status before Sunday; if he sits, Freddy's Dameon Pierce is on his bench. He also starts **Zay Flowers** (Lamar is on Freddy's IR; asked about DeVonta Smith for Flowers, Heath said "I would take Zay Flowers in a second," but doubted the deal happens if Lamar's return is near), **DK Metcalf** (leads the league in route participation but is "really bad in yards per route run"), **Jameson Williams** (the hosts' example of a boom-bust "worst case"), **Kelce**, **Bijan** and **Rodgers**. In the rapid-fire round both hosts took **Caleb Williams over Rodgers "at the Saints."** Caleb then scored 22.1 on Thursday.

**DYNASTY: Amon A Boat! (Poncho), 3-3, vs Sloppy 2nd's**

**Freddy's DYNASTY (The Man in Jahmyr):** He left **Colston Loveland** (19.9 on TNF) and **Hunter Henry** (14.1) on his bench while starting **Harold Fannin**. Heath had Loveland "at like 16." That's 34 points of TEs sitting on the bench. He also benched **DeMario Douglas** (5.3, a correct sit). He starts **Goff** (the hosts took Goff over Caleb, and Goff and Love are their alternatives to Maye), **Tetairoa McMillan** (on Adam's list of WRs held to 12.5 or fewer by the Bears) and **Gibbs**. **Terrance Ferguson** won't come off IR when first eligible, which is bad news for his bench stash.

summary: Jacob's Wednesday WR update is all usage. He moved A.J. Brown up to WR20 despite a 5.7-point game (22 XFP), raised Golden to WR14, dropped Garrett Wilson to WR18 and Michael Wilson to WR24, and called Coker and McMillan studs who help each other. Omar Cooper Jr. was his top waiver WR, Germie Bernard has a high-floor PPR role, and Christian Kirk and Ja'Kobi Lane are his stashes. For you, Coker and Worthy are both backed in MAIN, and Kirk and Lane are free. In dynasty, Shaheed is the shakiest start by his data, with Kupp the higher-floor bench option, and Odunze is a hold he's lukewarm on.

disagreements.text: No in-episode disagreements (solo show). He invites listeners to flip several pairs: Coker or McMillan up to the Nabers line, DeVonta Smith over Pickens, Metcalf over Waddle.

Cross-episode drift (BTBS vs BTBS): in this 10/21 episode Parker Washington sits just above Pickens (around WR12-13 by his description). Two days later, in the 10/23 "9 League-Winners" episode, he had Washington at ROS WR10 and Zay Flowers at WR6. Flowers here is only "extremely excited" inside WR1-13. Track both in the LW and WR7 rows.
Self-flagged tension: he ranks Waddle (WR27) over Metcalf (WR30) while admitting Metcalf is getting the role he wants for Waddle.

takeaways: Buy A.J. Brown on the 5.7-point game. 22 XFP is the biggest XFP-minus-FP gap for any WR game since 2021 in the FP Data model, with a 94% route rate in his first game back.
Hold or buy both Panthers WRs. Coker and McMillan's slot rates have converged (~37% each), and Jacob says they help each other.
Omar Cooper Jr. was his top waiver WR, with Germie Bernard right there (back-to-back elite XFP, 12 of 12 targets catchable).
Sell Garrett Wilson high if someone still pays a top-10 price. He's down to WR18 because the injuries that boosted his target share are healing.
Michael Wilson and Egbuka are usage-over-production buys, but Jacob trimmed Wilson to WR24.
Waddle at WR27 is a hold, not a dump; if you need points now, Jacob is fine flipping him for Diggs or someone in that range.
Avoid: DEN (except as a hope play), TEN beyond Tate, IND beyond Keenan Allen, SF WRs other than Evans, Mumpfield, Kupp and Barner outside deep leagues.
Cheap stashes: Christian Kirk (SF), Ja'Kobi Lane (BAL), Devontez Walker (BAL), Caleb Douglas (MIA), Ryan Flournoy (DAL), Harold Fannin Jr. (dynasty buy-low).
TE notes: Isaiah Likely is a WR in TE clothing; a Tucker Kraft bounce-back is "coming"; Loveland has been unlucky; Jake Ferguson's 50% route rate is a red flag.

title: RB Rest of Season Rankings I Week 7 Fantasy Football trade targets
hosts: solo. Dan Schneier is referenced but not on the episode.
summary: Jacob's Wednesday RB ROS update is all usage. His big movers are Tuten (now ahead of Jeanty), Hubbard (up 5 to RB10) and Kyren (RB8 and climbing). Charbonnet is his cheap sleeping-giant bell cow, and Mason is his favorite "points now" back. He's down on Jeanty's health, Jacobs (RB25), Rhamondre, Akers, and the DEN, NO, NYG and WAS backfields. For you, Mason, Ollie Gordon and JT are all backed. Kendre Miller is the weak link in your MAIN lineup. In dynasty, keep an eye on Breece Hall's status, with Braelon Allen behind him.

segments.title: Intro: a "Breeland" (Tuten) victory lap; show schedule (Tue and Thu 11 AM ET live with Dan Schneier; ROS rankings every Wednesday, one position at a time)
Running back analysis: Tuten's metrics, JAX run game, Chris Rodriguez
Usage deep dive: Zach Charbonnet's sleeping-giant case; Chuba Hubbard and Tuten as risers
Role trends: route participation and XFP leaders from Week 6
ROS rankings walkthrough, RB1 to about RB56
Break
Team-by-team usage, ARI through LV
Break
Team-by-team usage, LAC through WAS
Closing

disagreements.Other side: Dan Schneier "didn't feel like it was totally over" (relayed, 25:27)
The consensus market ("maybe that's too low," he concedes)

disagreements.Note: Same as the LW ep (Tuten RB11)

disagreements.Other side: Matches his SS7 stance vs Dan ([H2H-1024-3])

takeaways: Bhayshul Tuten is Jacob's top RB buy. Past-2-weeks XFP is RB7, Jeanty's snaps are fading, and LV's bye is late. He moved Tuten ahead of Jeanty.
Chuba Hubbard: ride him (ROS RB10). He played 93% of snaps with a 69% route rate, and the offense is now built around him.
Kyren Williams has a top-3 RB role on paper (#2 in XFP/g over 4 games). With Davante Adams out, the role may grow.
Zach Charbonnet is a cheap stash with bell-cow upside once he's back from the ACL. Jacob expects him to pass Rhamondre quickly and doesn't see Jadarian Price getting the valuable work.
Jordan Mason over Judkins and Saquon now. Ollie Gordon II gets the same nod. Aaron Jones loses value with Mason back.
Sell or fade Jeanty at name value unless his health turns. Rank Swift next to him.
Treat Jacobs as an RB3 until Green Bay's backfield shows it can produce.
Bucky Irving's value depends on Tampa's offense. The role (85% snaps) is good.
Stash Rico Dowdle and Travis Etienne Jr. (NO, IR). Ignore the DEN, NYG, NO (Kendre Miller is TD-only) and WAS backfields.
Dameon Pierce is a Week 7 flex (RB18 vs DAL MNF) only if you have to start him.

title: BDGE: "Ranking Every Week 7 Running Back as a Sit or Start" (Week 7 RB tiers)
summary: BDGE's Wednesday Week 7 RB rankings (solo, 28:39) put every back into five tiers. TNF already went his way: Swift (19.0 PPR) and Stevenson (22.5) hit, and Henderson, Kiner and Roschon flopped like he said. His Sunday calls to watch are Kenneth Walker going "nuts" vs SEA, Allgeier over Knight, Jacobs straight back into his role, and Jordan Mason held to 8-10 touches behind Aaron Jones. For Poncho, the flag is Jordan Mason in the MAIN lineup (only a shaky flex here). Walker, Taylor and Ollie Gordon look good, and Braelon Allen is the swap if Breece Hall sits in DYNASTY. Freddy has Pierce as cover if Saquon misses.

predictions.take: Corey Kiner doesn't earn a role over Stevenson
Jaylen Warren is a Must Start and stays the PIT workhorse over Dowdle
Lamar "not even close to a sure thing to play"
Woody Marks gets the majority of HOU RB touches vs NYG
Jordan Mason gets only 8-10 touches; Aaron Jones keeps a sizable chunk or the lead
Allgeier, not Knight, leads ARI's backfield
Josh Jacobs goes right back into his pre-suspension workhorse role
Kenneth Walker "is going to go f*ing nuts" vs SEA
Harbaugh might keep Skattebo benched; neither NYG RB is startable
Ollie Gordon is a Feels Good start vs NYJ

predictions.result: Push: Sleeper now lists him Out (knee, ACL), so he won't play

takeaways: Trust the volume backs: his Must Start list is Swift, Warren, Henry, Bijan, CMC, Chuba, Bucky, J. Taylor, Gibbs, Kyren, Kenneth Walker, Javonte. TNF already backed up the Swift and Stevenson calls.
Don't rush Jordan Mason back. He sees 8-10 touches and has Aaron Jones as the better (dub flex) start. That matters for Poncho's MAIN lineup (see below).
Breece Hall is the swing: if he plays he's only a dub flex, and Braelon Allen drops to shaky. If he sits, Allen "feels good." Wait for the Sunday inactive list.
Ollie Gordon and Woody Marks are confident starts in good matchups.
Avoid the Giants backfield completely, and don't trust any SEA back (Charbonnet is now Out anyway).
Allgeier over Knight in Arizona, while Love is out.
Jacobs: start him if you have him, but expect inefficiency behind a bottom-two OL.
Stash Dylan Sampson in deep-bench leagues.
my_notes:
Rosters from a live Sleeper pull, Sat 10/24 ~7 PM ET. Starter/bench is how the lineups sit right now.

**MAIN LEAGUE: Taylor Snift (Poncho)**

**DYNASTY: Amon A Boat! (Poncho)**

**Freddy, MAIN: Flowers for Ms. Jackson**
- **Bijan** (starter): Must Start. **Saquon** (starter, Questionable hamstring): "definitely don't think it's a definite" he plays. Freddy owns **Dameon Pierce**, the host's Dub Flex if Saquon sits, so he's covered. **Rico Dowdle**: Shaky Flex. **Kaelon Black**: Rather Not.

**Freddy, DYNASTY: The Man in Jahmyr**
- **Gibbs** and **Kyren** (starters): both Must Starts. **Blake Corum**: "you could definitely do worse at the flex spot." **TreVeyon Henderson**: Shaky Flex, and TNF proved it (4.3 PPR). **Jaylen Wright**: Rather Not. **Dylan Sampson**: stash. **Emmett Johnson / Raheim Sanders**: not discussed.

title: Week 7 Waiver Wire - Five Names Worth Your FAAB
url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qOG7KeePkSk · Runtime: 34:49 · Sponsors: Farmers Insurance (Josh's "game plan" segment), DraftKings (promo code read)
summary: Josh Norris and guest Joel Smyth called this "the worst waiver wire of the season" (34:49). Their top add is **Omar Cooper Jr.** (51 of 62 snaps, WR6), then **Ja'Kobi Lane** (red-zone role) and **Jaylin Noel**. Tre Tucker, Germie Bernard and Malik Washington come first anywhere they're still free. At RB, Kendre Miller is a stash, Mike Washington Jr. is a Jeanty handcuff and Zonovan Knight is outplaying Allgeier, while the Giants backfield is a full avoid. Michael Mayer is a TE streamer. In superflex, take McCarthy for the long run and McKee for one week vs Dallas. Drop Tyreek Hill, Jonathan Brooks and Makai Lemon. For you, it backs the Cooper bid in MAIN and keeps Kendre Miller in your Week 7 flex.

takeaways: Omar Cooper Jr. is the top add (#1 for both hosts). He played 51 of 62 snaps, and Josh thinks he can take Adonai Mitchell's job. Josh would bid 10-12% of budget, and Joel less than that.
The three "obvious" adds come first if they're free: Tre Tucker (WR2 in Week 6), Germie Bernard and Malik Washington.
Ja'Kobi Lane is #2: a red-zone receiver who gets better when Lamar returns. Josh would only go 5-10% FAAB.
Noel is #3: efficient and catches everything, but he's only on half the snaps.
RBs are thin. Kendre Miller is a stash (bye in Week 8, then a soft schedule), Mike Washington is a Jeanty handcuff, and Zonovan Knight is outplaying Allgeier. Avoid the Giants backfield.
Michael Mayer is a real TE streamer: LV is in 2-TE sets 66% of the time, the most in the league.
Superflex: McCarthy for the rest of the season, McKee as a one-week play vs Dallas.
Drops: Tyreek Hill, Jonathan Brooks, Makai Lemon and BTJ (in redraft).

summary: Josh, Hayden and Matt Harmon ran their 2½-hour Week 7 Stats vs. Film. Hayden's re-draft top six is Gibbs, Walker, Bijan, JSN, Puka and Amon-Ra. The biggest calls: buy George Pickens after the Eagles game, start Tyler Higbee as a top-12 TE with Adams out, add Antonio Williams (Hayden), Omar Cooper (Matt) and Travis Hunter, and avoid the Giants and Seahawks backfields. TNF already graded a few of them. Loveland was "for real" (7/12-69-1), Hayden's "complicated" NE backfield read beat Kiner hype (Rhamondre 22.5 PPR, Kiner 1.3), and Hayden's Jeremiyah Love return call is dead (he's Out). One cited stat failed the Sleeper check: Lawrence's "19+ in 13 straight." For you, the episode backs keeping Kendre Miller, Mason, Worthy and Coker in MAIN. In DYNASTY, watch Breece's quad (Braelon is the fallback), and Keenan Allen looks like your weakest starter.

title: Sal Vetri: "5 Players I'm Panicking About in Fantasy Football" (Week 6 panic meter)
summary: Sal's Week 6 panic meter rates seven players. **Full panic** on **Cam Skattebo** (0 carries, 6 snaps, benched for fumbles; bench every Giants RB) and **Jaylen Waddle** (a 30% target share wasted by Bo Nix's 4.0 Y/A and 4.9 aDOT). **No panic** on **A.J. Brown** (97% routes, 10 targets, drops; "set for a big Thursday Night Football") and **Jaylen Warren** (74% snaps; Dowdle's hot first half was "fear-mongering"; top-15 RB ROS). **Moderate** on **Josh Downs** (needs 10 targets in a checkdown offense), **4/10** on **Bucky Irving** (elite role, no efficiency), and **7/10** on **Michael Wilson** (screen-heavy, tough schedule; Bourne is a flex add). For Poncho: Sal calls **Tyler Warren's** groin a likely multi-week absence, so swap **Keenan Allen** into that DYN slot, and fill MAIN's empty FLEX with **Kendre Miller**.

segments.title: Cold open: whether to panic, "full on panic," or make a move
Cam Skattebo / Giants backfield: 0 carries, 6 snaps, fumbles, Glazer's "Najee starts" report, five-RB committee. Full panic
Jaylen Waddle / Bo Nix: 30% target share for 4/24, aDOT 4.9 joke, WR52, 646-yard pace, Payton's quote. Full panic
Recording-time note (Mon noon ET); R.J. Harvey's checkdowns
A.J. Brown: 97% routes, 34% target share, 2-4 drops (a likely 60-yd TD), Doubs AC joint → "big Thursday Night Football." No panic
DraftKings ad
Josh Downs: no Pierce or Tyler Warren (late scratch, groin), Keenan Allen's 12 targets, game log since Pierce's injury, Daniel Jones' struggles. Moderate panic
Subscribe ask ("over 60%… are not subscribed")
Bucky Irving: 21 touches for 49 yards, 85% snaps / 90% rush share, backup QB, Baker's thumb, last year's 10.2 PPG split. 4/10
Ad for his free start/sit tool (fantasyfootballstarts.com): Mike Evans 17.2 vs Terry McLaurin 11.2 projection demo
Jaylen Warren vs Rico Dowdle: first-half 54% Dowdle opportunity share was "fear-mongering"; final 74% snaps, 66/33 carry split. No panic
Michael Wilson vs Kendrick Bourne: 4 of 7 targets were screens, McBride's NFL record, Bourne's 64 yds / 8 targets as a starter, tough schedule. 7/10
Wrap and plug for his waiver video

format: Solo panic-meter video. Each player gets a panic grade, sometimes as a number (Bucky 4/10, Wilson 7/10), with a built-in "it depends on your expectations" hedge for Downs, Bucky and Wilson.
tone and emotion: Disgusted and sarcastic about the Giants and Broncos ("disgusting" about seven times, "Sure." at Harbaugh's denial, the Bo Nix name joke). Protective of A.J. Brown and Jaylen Warren, calling the Warren panic "fear-mongering for no reason." Measured on Bucky.
bullish: A.J. Brown ("big Thursday Night Football"), Jaylen Warren (top-15 RB ROS), Kendrick Bourne (bye-week flex), Bucky's role, Rodgers' passing volume.
bearish: Cam Skattebo and the whole Giants backfield (no adds, no trades, no starts), Jaylen Waddle and Bo Nix ("this offense is broken"), Josh Downs and the Daniel Jones checkdown offense, Michael Wilson as a WR2, R.J. Harvey's checkdowns.
method notes: Route % vs target share (Brown 97% / 34%, Waddle 80% / 30%), snap and rush share (Bucky 85/90, Warren 74/63/55), first-half vs full-game splits (Dowdle), game logs with a big game removed (Waddle ex-Wk2), "points left on the field" from drops (~7 for Brown), and schedule strength (Wilson's next 5).

Today: "full panic," not in his top 30-36 RBs, "lost his coach's trust." His snap-count prediction stands, but his start/sit view flipped to never start

disagreements.Arguments: Schneier: best Giants RB on tape. Sal: "I don't want to add Tyron Tracy" (consistent with his "fool's gold" call yesterday)

disagreements.Arguments: They lean sell / decline watch. Sal doubles down: no panic, "big Thursday Night Football"

Yesterday "extremely consistent." Today he's only useful if he catches 7-8+ balls in a checkdown offense. That's a softer tone

predictions.take: A.J. Brown "is set for a big Thursday Night Football" in Wk7 vs CHI (grade: ≥15 PPR = hit)
Jaylen Warren is a top-15 RB rest of season, not top-5 (grade: PPR RB rank Wks 7-17)
No Giants RB in his Wk7 top 30-36; Skattebo can't be started "moving forward" (grade: Skattebo under 10 PPR in Wk7-8 = hit)
Waddle can't be started; nothing changes under Bo Nix (grade: Waddle outside top-36 PPR WR Wks 7-10 = hit)
Josh Downs is only relevant in 10-target games; no explosive plays (grade: Downs under 12 PPR/game Wks 7-10 = hit)
Bucky Irving is a "matchup dependent RB2 / flex," not an elite RB (grade: RB13-30 PPR Wks 7-10 = hit)
Michael Wilson ranks WR20-30 weekly, a WR2/3 flex (grade: avg PPR WR rank Wks 7-11)
ARI's next 5 (DEN, DAL, SEA, LAR, KC) give Wilson only one good matchup (DAL) (grade: Wilson's best game is vs DAL = hit)
Tyler Warren's groin is "usually a multi-week absence" (grade: misses Wk7 and Wk8 = hit)
If Baker returns Wk7 he won't be near 100% and Bucky's efficiency stays muted (grade: Bucky under 4.0 YPC in Wk7 = hit)

takeaways: Bench every Giants RB, Skattebo included, and don't add Tracy, Najee or Singletary. Sal wouldn't trade for any of them either.
Don't start Jaylen Waddle in Bo Nix's offense (aDOT 4.9, 4.0 Y/A). Hold him in 12+ team leagues; he's droppable only in shallow 10-teamers.
Start A.J. Brown with confidence in Wk7 (97% routes, 10 targets, Doubs likely out). It's Sal's most confident call.
Keep starting Jaylen Warren (74% snaps). Dowdle's first half was noise, so Dowdle is a handcuff, not a flex.
Bucky Irving = RB2/flex, not a sell-in-a-panic. The role is elite, but efficiency is capped until Baker is healthy.
Downgrade the Colts' WRs under Daniel Jones. Downs needs 10 targets, and Keenan Allen only pays in PPR when he catches 7-8+.
Tyler Warren may miss multiple weeks (groin). Plan around him.
Michael Wilson is a WR3/flex with a tough next five. Kendrick Bourne is a live bye-week flex add.

title: Who to Add for Week 7? Waiver Wire Targets, Streamers & Must-Have Pickups | 2026 Fantasy Football
summary: A 44-minute Tuesday podcast (Adam, Jamey, Dave), separate from the morning livestream. **Rachaad White** is still the #1 add despite the bye. **Omar Cooper Jr.** is Dave's WR pick and Jamey's long-term pick, and **DeMario Douglas** is the better Week 7 start. Jamey streams **Kyler Murray** and **Rodgers** "right away," while Dave would start **Kirk Cousins** over both. At TE it's **Hunter Henry** (Jamey) vs **Kyle Pitts** then Higbee (Dave). Dave says cut **MarShawn Lloyd** for **Pierre Strong** and grab **Tyrone Tracy** if White is gone, and **Kendre Miller** is again a "trap back." Adam's tip: **Will Reichard** is 15-for-15. Dave won "Who Has More?". Nearly every stat checked out against Sleeper; the one miss was Adam's Concepcion "9, 8, 6 targets in his last three" (Week 5 was 1). For you, Poncho: in MAIN, Cooper, Douglas, Henry, Pitts, Murray and Reichard are all free, and your starter Kendre got called a trap again. In DYNASTY, you own White and Rodgers, and Douglas, Murray, Tracy and Pierre Strong are free. Freddy starts MarShawn Lloyd (the show's top drop) and has Henry, Ferguson, Reichard and Gibbs rotting on his bench.

takeaways: Rachaad White is still the #1 RB add even on bye; in DYNASTY you already own him, so plan to start him Wks 8–10.
Omar Cooper Jr. is the best long-term WR add, and DeMario Douglas the best Week 7 start (Thursday vs CHI). Both are free in MAIN; Douglas is free in DYNASTY.
Kyler Murray (free in both of your leagues) is the cleanest QB stream; Dave would start Cousins first.
At TE, Hunter Henry (Jamey) and Kyle Pitts (Dave) are both free in MAIN, and both beat your current TE production.
Cut MarShawn Lloyd for Pierre Strong (Dave), and use Tyrone Tracy as the fallback if White is gone.
Kendre Miller is a "need nine points" flex vs PIT, nothing more.
Cheap stashes: Terrance Ferguson (eligible next week), Jordan Tyson, Konata Mumpfield, Samaje Perine.
Kicker: Will Reichard is 15-for-15 and free in MAIN.

title: Week 7 Waiver Wire: MUST ADD Players, Injury Replacements & Streamers | 2026 Fantasy Football Advice
summary: A 69-minute Week 7 waiver show with Adam, Jamey and Dave, one day after Jamey's 50th. **Rachaad White** is the consensus #1 add despite the Wk7 bye (low-end RB2 for three games, up to 20% FAB). **Omar Cooper Jr.** (~15%) and **DeMario Douglas** (<10%) are the WR adds; Douglas is the better Week 7 start and Cooper the better hold. At TE, Jamey wants **Hunter Henry**, Dave wants **Michael Mayer** and a **Terrance Ferguson** stash, and **Kyle Pitts** is the upside play. **Kyler Murray** and **Rodgers** are the streaming QBs, the **Browns** the top DST, and the **Kendre Miller** fight ends with "only if you're desperate." Every stat checked against Sleeper held up except Jamey's McLaughlin goal-line TD (it didn't happen in Wk6) and a couple of small counting slips. For you, Poncho: MAIN has a bye-week hole (Hampton plus an empty slot) and Cooper, Douglas, Pitts, Henry and Murray are all free there. In DYNASTY, Hockenson and Warren are both Out, so pivot to Keenan Allen. Freddy is hoarding Henry and Ferguson on his DYNASTY bench, and his MAIN starters (Cousins, Juwan, Vele) got roasted.

takeaways: Rachaad White is the consensus #1 add, even on a Wk7 bye. Expect 11–15 touches and a low-end RB2 role for three games (PHI, LAR, @NYG). FAB "20%… max."
Cooper (~15% FAB) and Douglas (<10%) are the WR adds. Douglas is the better Wk7 start (CHI on TNF; MIA almost never allows big WR target counts). Cooper is the better long-term hold.
TE: Hunter Henry has the safest floor (three straight 11+). Kyle Pitts (15.2, 23.0) is the upside play if he's free. Stash Terrance Ferguson with LAR's Adams out 6–10 weeks.
QB for byes (Allen, Lawrence, Daniels, Herbert): Kyler Murray (IND, then great schedule) and Rodgers (@NO) over Cousins; Penix is a low-end starter.
RB: Only start Kendre Miller if you're desperate. Stash Tracy and Jonah Coleman. Pierre Strong only if Jacobs sits; McLaughlin only if Judkins sits.
Drops for Wk7: Bills WRs (not DJ Moore), Josh Downs, Wan'Dale Robinson, Tre Tucker, Devaughn Vele (NO bye Wk8), Dalton Schultz. Keep Keenan Allen and Brenton Strange.
DST: Browns @TEN first; 49ers, Jets, Cardinals; Texans and Vikings if available. K: Reichard, Boswell, McPherson.
my_notes:
**MAIN LEAGUE: Taylor Snift (Poncho, 2-4).** Week 7 is the Freddy matchup.

**DYNASTY: Amon A Boat! (Poncho, 3-3)**

**Freddy (FreddyB2)**
- **MAIN, Flowers for Ms. Jackson (2-4), your Week 7 opponent:** His starters got rough reviews. **Kirk Cousins**: "brutal" schedule starting with the Rams, and the hosts would start Murray and Rodgers over him this week (with a "wheels are falling off" worry). **Juwan Johnson** got a 0 and a 5 on the Drop-O-Meter after 5.6 and 0.0. **Devaughn Vele** got "a sad goodbye," with NO on bye next week. **Dameon Pierce** is his best piece (15.0 PPR, plus Carson Steele's shoulder). He has the better QB (Rodgers, vs NO) on his bench. **Saquon** "didn't practice at all."
- **DYNASTY, The Man in Jahmyr (3-3):** Freddy has **both of the show's top TE targets on his bench**: Jamey's #1 add **Hunter Henry** and Dave's #1 stash **Terrance Ferguson**. He starts **MarShawn Lloyd**, whom Jamey would "move on from," and **Harold Fannin** (Drop-O-Meter 5). **Germie Bernard** is the show's "number one player to add" in shallow leagues, and he already has him. **Kendrick Bourne** got the "safe floor, not a high ceiling" label.

**Your-teams bottom line:** In MAIN you have a real hole this week (Hampton bye plus an empty slot), and the wire has what you need: Cooper, Douglas, Pitts, Henry and Murray. In DYNASTY, sit Hockenson and Warren (both Out on Sleeper) and lean on Keenan Allen. White is your post-bye payoff.

summary: A 50-minute hot-takes episode with Jacob Gibbs and RotoWire's Theo Gremminger, all rest-of-season calls: Worthy as a WR24-30 while Rice is out, Tuten top-10 RB, Loveland back to a top-5 TE, Bryce Young top-10 QB, Zay Flowers top-5 (Jacob) or top-8 (Theo), Bernard top-30 WR, Bucky back to top-15, and J.J. McCarthy top-18 QB. Almost every countable stat checked out against Sleeper. For you, Poncho, it's good news on Worthy (Rice is out for Week 7), a nudge to start LaPorta over a "cooked" Mark Andrews, Kenneth Walker getting cornerstone treatment in Dynasty, and McCarthy sitting free in both leagues. Freddy's Zay Flowers got the biggest hype, but it all depends on Lamar's ankle.

my_notes:
**MAIN, Taylor Snift (PPR + first downs; 70.75 in Wk7 so far).** You're starting Kendre Miller (Jacob's top waiver RB; 5.8 so far) and Xavier Worthy (a riser for both, but KC's implied total is just 20 at SEA). Jalen Coker got Dan's "massive win" nod (1.9 so far). Omarion Hampton on your bench is a "role up, don't buy" guy, so he's a hold, not a starter. Stefon Diggs (bench) gets the red-zone and third-down "souped-up Downs" role now that McLaurin is out, which fits first-down scoring once WAS is off bye. Davante Adams on IR opens the Rams door for Mumpfield and T. Ferguson (Ferguson is now on IR too, per Sleeper).

**DYNASTY, Amon A Boat! (full PPR; 57.28 so far).** Rome Odunze (10.9 on TNF) is the guy both hosts said has too few chances. Rodgers (13.08 so far) was Jacob's second-tier stream, and Dan leaned Geno. Kenneth Walker is on Dan's "wouldn't trade for CMC" list. Tank Dell on your bench is expected to be eased in (Jacob said about 5 routes); he has 1 catch for 43 yards so far. Trevor Lawrence (bench) was Wk6's QB1, and Dan says JAX's run and pass games are finally clicking. Quentin Johnston and Brenen Thompson are on the team Dan called "totally shot." Breece Hall being out has helped Braelon, and Jacob ranked Braelon top-12.

**Yahoo HE-MAN'S HEROES.** McConkey (Out) is a faller for both. D'Andre Swift's role didn't change without Monangai, though Roschon took 40% of snaps (Swift had 19.0 on TNF). Josh Jacobs is "top-20 easily," but Pierre Strong may take passing downs. Herbert on your bench: Dan is "out on Herbert."

**Yahoo He-Man's New Super Flex.** Waddle has slid to Jacob's WR3 range. Penix (19.88 so far) was a hard "no" from Dan. Pitts (bench, 13.2 so far) isn't a buy for Dan. Lamar should be back soon, which they say boosts Zay Flowers.

title: A Week to Take Advantage of Your Idiot Leaguemates on Waivers
summary: Michael O'Hara's Week 7 BDGE waiver show says the RB pool is "really brutal" and the value is at WR and TE stashes. His top stash is Terrance Ferguson, followed by Jonah Coleman, Travis Hunter and Dylan Sampson, and Keenan Allen and DeMario Douglas are his plug-and-play flexes. He's cooler than the market on Omar Cooper Jr. ("more of a bench stash") and Mumpfield, and he says to drop BTJ, Sutton, Lloyd and Keaton Mitchell. For Poncho, the show supports the DYNASTY claims on Kyler and Douglas and says to flex Keenan Allen. In MAIN it's a mild caution against raising the Cooper bid. Freddy owns both of Michael's favorite stashes (Ferguson and Sampson), and two of his starters (Lloyd and Sutton) are on the drop list.

segments.title: Intro. "If you need a running back this week, good luck because it's really brutal"
QB targets: C.J. Stroud (0:30), Kyler Murray (0:45), Michael Penix (2:09)
Superflex QBs: Tanner McKee (4:17), J.J. McCarthy (5:26)
RB targets: Roschon Johnson (6:59), Kendre Miller (9:50), Jaleel McLaughlin (12:25), Dylan Sampson (13:54), Tyrone Tracy (14:58), Samaje Perine (16:57), Jonah Coleman (18:15)
WR targets: Omar Cooper Jr. (20:15), Keenan Allen (22:13), Travis Hunter (23:13), Jaylin Noel (25:33), Ja'Kobi Lane (27:27), Konata Mumpfield (28:33), Antonio Williams (30:18)
WR "roster band-aids": DeMario Douglas (31:48), Brandin Cooks (33:14), Christian Kirk (34:41)
TE targets: Tyler Higbee & Hunter Henry (35:21), Terrance Ferguson (36:04), Chig Okonkwo (38:06), Michael Mayer (39:06)
Trending drops: MarShawn Lloyd, Keaton Mitchell, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Emanuel Wilson (RB); Darius Cooper, Courtland Sutton, Brian Thomas Jr., Dontayvion Wicks (WR)
Outro

disagreements.Details: Michael: "more of a bench stash," won't out-target Garrett Wilson, and Adonai Mitchell muddies it. FFT's Jamey called him the "headliner," Hayden says every 12-team league, and Poncho's MAIN plan bids $121. Nick (BDGE-1) was also "hesitant," so BDGE is consistently cooler
#3 trending add (+410k on Sleeper per the 10/20 waiver intel); Michael: "not as much of a slam dunk" because of 13 personnel; 5–7% FAAB
Michael: don't let 18.5 PPR fool you; Skattebo's benching is "a slap on the wrist." Dan (FFT) was bullish; Sal called it fool's gold, which matches Michael
Michael: Skattebo likely "leads the backfield next week." Nick (BDGE-1): "You just got to take the L"

Michael: "the primary ball carrier… moving forward," but "not that good." FFT: "clear goal-line back." Nick (BDGE-1): three-way split. Michael is the most bullish BDGE voice on role, and the least bullish on talent
Michael: return "as early as this week" and a real job threat. Nick: gets rolling around Wks 9–11
Michael: stash, everything moving his way. Sal: "too valuable on defense." (Matches Nick's add)
Michael: stash him right now, the #1 TE pickup. Nick: only if Adams misses multiple weeks (Adams is now out 6–10 weeks, so Nick's condition is met)

predictions.take: Skattebo "comes back and leads the backfield next week" (Wk 7)
Terrance Ferguson becomes "basically… the wide receiver 2 behind Nacua" once he returns (eligible Wk 8)
Jonah Coleman challenges and can "straight up steal" Dobbins' lead job
Dylan Sampson is CLE's 1A over McLaughlin and Estimé whenever he's active and Judkins sits
Kendre Miller stays NO's primary ball carrier until Kamara is healthy
McCarthy is named NYG's starter "soon"
Omar Cooper won't out-target Garrett Wilson week to week ("No chance")
Keenan Allen keeps a 9+ target floor, especially with Warren out
Jaylin Noel's role expands from his 51% route rate
Mumpfield's role is limited by heavy 13 personnel without Adams
Mike Evans misses Wk 7
Brian Thomas Jr. stays droppable, with no fantasy-relevant role unless traded
DeMario Douglas is a usable short-term flex until Brown, Hollins and Doubs are back

takeaways: Terrance Ferguson (LAR TE, on IR): Michael's #1 stash ("go stash him on your IR slot right now"), and Adams is out 6–10 weeks.
Jonah Coleman (DEN RB, IR): the strongest RB stash; Dobbins is at 3.3 YPC ✅.
Keenan Allen is "the epitome of a spot start in your flex": 9+ targets for three straight games ✅, more if Warren sits.
DeMario Douglas is a short-term flex on TNF @CHI (19.6 and 22.5 PPR in Wks 5–6 ✅).
Kyler Murray is the 1QB streamer for the soft stretch (IND, DET, BUF); Penix is a coin-flip stream vs SF.
Stashes: Travis Hunter, Dylan Sampson (free), Ja'Kobi Lane, Antonio Williams, Jaylin Noel, Perine.
Spot RBs only if desperate: Roschon (6–8% FAAB, TNF), Kendre Miller, McLaughlin. Avoid Tracy.
Cooper Jr. is a bench stash with WR2 upside vs MIA; don't expect him to out-target Garrett Wilson.
Drops: BTJ, Sutton, Lloyd, Keaton Mitchell, Croskey-Merritt (IR), Emanuel Wilson, Darius Cooper, Wicks.
my_notes:
**MAIN LEAGUE: Taylor Snift (Poncho)**

**DYNASTY: Amon A Boat! (Poncho)**

**Freddy, MAIN: Flowers for Ms. Jackson**
- **Keaton Mitchell** (bench): "an easy drop."
- **Saquon / Pierce:** McKee is PHI's QB for the year, with "really, really poor" efficiency, which hurts the whole PHI offense.
- **Kirk Cousins:** Michael expects LV to "rack up some pass volume" vs LAR (the Mayer section). **Bijan:** the Penix TD coin-flip cuts into Bijan's goal-line TDs. **Zay Flowers:** Lane is lining up as the WR2 behind him once Lamar returns. **Vele / Juwan Johnson:** the NO offense "has not been effective." **Jakobi Meyers:** JAX is pushing its depth WRs (BTJ) out. **Jaguars DEF:** not discussed.

**Freddy, DYNASTY: The Man in Jahmyr**
- **MarShawn Lloyd** (his RB starter): "easy drop" now that Jacobs is back. That's the second show today to say so.
- **Terrance Ferguson** (his bench, IR): Michael's #1 TE stash, so Freddy owns the guy this show wants most.
- **Dylan Sampson** (his bench, IR): Michael's preferred CLE back once he's active. Another Freddy win.
- **Courtland Sutton** (his starter): "Straight up awful… easy drop."
- **Hunter Henry** (his bench): worth a pickup. **Fannin / Raheim Sanders:** CLE's backfield goes McLaughlin → Sampson. **Kyren / Corum / Stafford / Ty Simpson:** LAR goes heavy 13 personnel without Adams. **Jaxson Dart (IR):** NYG might hand McCarthy the job. **Addison:** a Kyler "cupcake" stretch helps. **Deebo (Out):** Evans is out too, so Cooks and Kirk soak up routes.

takes.detail: "Rostered in 60% of sleeper leagues… The guy has straight up been hooping"

Completion rate "pretty high," but production and efficiency lag. "Cupcake schedule coming up" (IND, DET, BUF D's "outright horrific"). Wk 5 vs NO: 51 rush yds ✅ (24/30, 229, 1 TD, 10 car). Best in Wks 8–9 when opponents force dropbacks

ATL scoring well with him (claims ~45 vs GB, 23 vs BAL/CHI; team scores not checked). 1 pass TD in each of his first three starts ✅ (Wks 3–5), then 3 TDs vs CHI in catch-up mode ✅ (225 yds, 23.1). TD split vs Bijan / B-Rob is "a scratchoff lottery ticket." Wk 7 vs SF should force dropbacks

Starter "for either the entire season or the foreseeable future"; Hurts (blood clots) expected out for the year. First start: 45 att ✅, 26 cmp ✅, 215 yds ✅. EPA/play "really, really poor" ❓. Wk 7 vs DAL is "attackable"

243 yds, TD, INT ✅. "17 fantasy points in the fourth quarter" (Sleeper total 17.32 ✅; the Q4 split isn't checkable). Played "roughly 11 minutes." Doesn't change his long-term view ("larger sample… just frankly horrible"), but Harbaugh "has a decision to make"

Monangai has missed 2 straight; estimated DNP Monday on a short week (TNF vs NE). ~40% snaps both weeks ✅ (27/69, 31/77). Wk 5: 7 tgt, 5 rec ✅. Wk 6: 13 car ✅, 2 tgt ✅, TD ✅; 8 of 13 carries came in Q4 garbage time, and he went down at the 1 to ice it. "It's a gross one"

Travis Etienne on IR. Since Kamara's back injury: 44.4% snaps ✅ (32/72) and 20 carries ✅ in Wk 6; 4 of 5 inside-the-5 carries over two weeks ❓. YPC 3.0 / 3.5 ✅. "He's not that good," but "15 carries, 75 yards… and punches in a score" is the serviceable story. Primary ball carrier "until either [Etienne] returns or Alvin Kamara is good to go"
Hurt his back in Wk 4, aggravated it diving for a pass in Wk 6; "they don't want to just ram [him] into the line." Watch practice
Lead back with Judkins out: 63% snaps ✅ (39/62), 9 car ✅, 4 tgt ✅. Lost the lone goal-line carry to Aaric Estimé; "5'7, 187 pounds." Wk 7 @TEN is "relatively stout"
Limited practices last week before being ruled out; "just straight up a better player" than McLaughlin or Estimé. "My preferred option in deeper leagues… the 1A should Judkins miss." Get him for $0

Skattebo benched: 6 snaps ✅, 0 touches ✅. Snaps: Tracy 30 (Sleeper 29 ⚠️), Singletary 26 (Sleeper 31 ⚠️), Harris 11. 8 touches ✅, 45 scrimmage yds ✅, 2 TDs ✅, 38% snaps ✅, 18.5 PPR ✅. "I'm not going to let the box score… play too many tricks on me"
"Most likely it was a slap on the wrist. He comes back and leads the backfield next week"
CIN had a Wk 6 bye. Wk 5: 14 car ✅ at 4.8 YPC ✅ (68 yds) with goal-line work. "8% rostered" ❓. 1A/1B or handcuff value

Dobbins "3.3 yards per carry" ✅ (270 yds on 81 carries). "His job is anything but safe." Coleman could be back "as early as this week"; "one of the few situations where… a rookie… just straight up steal[s] someone's job." Stash in IR

Wk 1: one route, 30-yd catch ✅, then ankle sprain and IR. Wk 6 return: 82% snaps ✅ (51/62), 81.8% route rate ❓, 23.3% target share ❓, 7 tgt ✅, 0.26 TPRR ❓, 6/103/1 ✅ (48-yd TD from Geno). Won't out-target Garrett Wilson ("No chance"); Adonai Mitchell's return "further muddies the waters." Could start vs MIA, "but I think this is more of a bench stash"
takes.take: Add / Stash (WR2 vs MIA if AD out)

takes.detail: 9+ targets in each of his last three games ✅ (9/9/11) and 15+ PPR in two of them ✅ (18.3, 16.2). Better path if Tyler Warren sits. Daniel Jones "has been turbo dog [] this year," but Allen gets there on volume. "The epitome of a spot start in your flex"

7 routes ❓, 16.3% route rate ❓ (both season highs), 4 tgt, 4/59/1 ✅ (Sleeper 9 snaps). "Arguably even a high-end elite route runner." BTJ played zero second-half snaps; Coen: "guys just got to make plays." "Very, very comfortable stashing him"
0 second-half snaps in Wk 6 (Sleeper: 15 of 71 snaps for the game). No catch since Wk 4 ✅ (0 rec on 5 targets, Wks 5–6). "Dropable. Dropable." Hold only in deep leagues, hoping for a trade

107 yds and a TD in Wk 6 ✅; TD in Wk 5 ✅; a 50-yd catch in Wk 4 (85 yds that day ✅). 15.9 PPR/game over 3 weeks ✅ (11.9 / 15.2 / 20.7). 2.69 YPRR, 6th among WRs with 100+ routes ❓. Season route rate 51.2% ❓, never 65% in a game (Sleeper snap share tops out at 62%, consistent). Hutchinson, Booty, MHJ and Tank Dell all crowd the room

First game since his Wk 1 fractured wrist: 55.3% route rate ❓, 5 tgt / 4 rec / 40 yds ✅, 8 PPR ✅. "The training camp of a lifetime." Could be "the clear-cut secondary pass catcher behind Zay Flowers" once Lamar returns

Adams out "six to 10 weeks" with "a ruptured hamstring" (Sleeper lists Adams Out, Knee ⚠️). LAR in 12/13 personnel on 40.5% of plays ❓; per JJ Zachary (Late-Round Fantasy), 13 personnel on 86% of snaps without Adams ❓. "Not as much of a slam dunk"; 5–7% FAAB

Wk 1 4/64/1 ✅. An 87-yd TD called back in Wk 4 (illegal shift). McLaurin "seemingly pretty serious leg injury" on MNF; Williams led WAS with 35 routes on 47 Daniels dropbacks ❓, but only 4 targets ✅. WAS has a bye: "light a roster spot on fire for the week"

A.J. Brown "knocking the rust off," Doubs on IR, Hollins banged up. 74.2% routes ❓, 26.7% target share ❓, 86 yds + TD ✅, 19.6 PPR ✅. Volatile targets "seven, two, five, eight" (Sleeper Wks 1–6: 7, 2, 5, 3, 5, 8). TNF @CHI shootout

Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis) "will almost certainly miss week seven," then the SF bye in Wk 8. Cooks: 16 routes, 1 target after Evans left ❓ (Sleeper: 2 targets for the game). Offense flows through CMC (10 targets) and Kittle
"Maybe going to make his return in week seven," per Shanahan (calf IR). Lots of routes if active, but don't be aggressive
50%+ rostered. "Expect Higbee to run a ton of routes" until Ferguson returns (eligible Wk 8)
5 tgt / 4 rec / TD ✅ in Wk 6; benefits from the banged-up NE WRs; TNF @CHI

IR (ankle). "This is the guy to pick up and target… the primary beneficiary of the Davante Adams injury." 6'5", 250. 42% slot / 16.7% wide routes ❓; 0.29 TPRR ❓. "Basically… the wide receiver 2 behind Nacua." "Go stash him on your IR slot right now"
Full-time role after McLaurin went down: 41 routes on 47 dropbacks ❓, 7 targets ✅ (7/69). "A really talented player… [after] the catch." Bye in Wk 7, so only if you have room
16 PPR ✅ (7/95). Bowers plays like a WR, so Mayer runs routes, but "incredibly volatile" next to Jeanty and Tre Tucker. A fringe TE1 vs LAR
Dinged early in Wk 6 (Sleeper 1.0 PPR ✅). "Now that Josh Jacobs is making his return, that is an easy drop"
"Any optimism about the Chargers offense has been wiped away"; bye in Wk 7. "An easy drop" (Wk 6: 0.4 PPR ✅)
14 PPR breakout in Wk 5 ✅ (14.2); now on IR (groin), out four weeks
Role cut by Holani in Wk 6 (Sleeper 27 of 85 snaps); Price and Charbonnet eligible to return. "Those times are done"
"The mirage… has come to an end" with McKee at QB (Wk 6 1/9 ✅)
"Straight up awful this year." Easy drop in 10-team and shallow 12-team leagues
Same McKee downgrade. Can drop

title: Yahoo: Josh & Hayden: "Fantasy Football Week 6 Recap - We Keep Winning"
url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lJQPIjlEJus · Runtime: 1:45:19 · Sponsors: Farmers Insurance, DraftKings (promo segment ~0:26, ~0:50)
summary: Josh, Hayden and Matt Harmon went through all 11 Sunday-afternoon games in 1:45. Their biggest calls: JJ McCarthy will start more games than Winston ("a guarantee"); Coker and McMillan are top-20 WRs the rest of the way; Omar Cooper Jr. should be rostered in every 12-team league; Pierce's role is too big to fail; and Kenneth Walker (19-128-2) belongs in the OPOY mix. Germie Bernard (11 catches, a Steelers rookie record) is the new PIT WR2. Chargers RBs combined for 43 yards and are unstartable. Kendre Miller owns the Saints backfield. Adams left late with a calf/possible pull, so watch him.

segments.title: Bears 31, Falcons 23 (Caleb back; Loveland, Burden, Swift/Roschon, Penix under pressure, Pitts)
Saints 34, Giants 27 (Winston benched → JJ McCarthy 17-pt 4th Q; Giants RB mess; Kendre Miller)
Farmers ad
Upset of the week: Cardinals 18, Rams 16 (no ARI TD; Stafford pressured; Bam Knight > Allgeier; Adams exits)
Panthers 25, Eagles 14 (Bryce/Brad Idzik, Hubbard 28 carries, Coker & McMillan, Eagles mess, Pierce, Hurts)
DraftKings ad

title: 10 Must Add Players to Pick Up in Your Fantasy League Right Now
summary: Sal's Week 7 waiver video is built around **adds vs fool's gold**. The clear #1 is **Germie Bernard** ("100% of my fab"). Next tier: **Ja'Kobi Lane**, who has red-zone equity with Lamar back and Bateman's AC joint hurt, and whom Sal prefers over **Kendre Miller** (20 carries but only 32/72 snaps, Etienne coming). Also **Kendrick Bourne** (bye-week flex), **Omar Cooper Jr.**, **DeMario Douglas** and **Malik Washington**. Stashes: **Dylan Sampson** (expected back Wk7), **Jaylin Noel** (14+ teams), **Bam Knight**, and handcuffs **Kaelon Black / Emmett Johnson / Brian Robinson**. Avoid **Tyrone Tracy** ("let your idiot league add" him), **Travis Hunter** ("too valuable on defense") and **Brian Thomas Jr.** ("unusable"). Don't sell **A.J. Brown** over his drops. Poncho: Sal is fading your Miller and backing this morning's waiver plan. Freddy owns half of Sal's list.

title: EARLY Week 7 Waiver Wire TARGETS! Cooper, Tyson, Tracy Jr, Murray, Henry, & Others! (FFT Express)
summary: A 10-minute early waiver episode on Jamey's 50th birthday. **Omar Cooper Jr.** is the headliner, though Adam worries about Adonai Mitchell's return and Garrett Wilson. **DeMario Douglas** is a low-FAB add, **Hunter Henry** is "the easy one" at TE, with **Mayer** behind him. For QBs, **Murray** and **Rodgers** are the Week 7 starters (slight nod Rodgers), and **McCarthy** is a must-add in 2QB/Superflex. RBs got a flat "No," with Tracy, Miller and Knight as the deep options. The **Vikings** are the #1 DST. Every stat checked out against Sleeper. For you, Poncho: the MAIN wire has Murray, Henry, Mayer, Cooper, Douglas and three of the four DSTs, which helps with Allen's bye and Andrews's slump. Freddy has Henry on his DYNASTY bench and Rodgers on his MAIN bench.

06:45–08:10 · Tight ends · Hunter Henry ("the easy one"), Michael Mayer, Colby Parkinson vs Tyler Higbee, Tommy Tremble.
08:10–09:59 · DST · Vikings (#1, vs IND), Browns (vs TEN), Jets over Dolphins, sneaky Cardinals (vs DEN). Adam's DST stat. Sign-off.

title: Week 6 Winners & Losers: Biggest Takeaways From Every Game! | 2026 Fantasy Football Advice
summary:
Four-man Winners & Losers after the 1 PM / 4 PM windows. **Jamey's winners** were waiver darling **Germie Bernard** and **Luther Burden**; **Heath's** were the tight end bounce-backs **Loveland** and **Pitts** (Pitts target share up four straight weeks to 21.2%). **Dave** crowned **Stroud** and **Bryce Young** must-start QBs and buried **Odunze** / **Michael Wilson**. Biggest loser energy: **Skattebo** (zero touches under Harbaugh), **Downs** still stuck, **Rhamondre** after Kiner's clock-kill package, and Adam sweating **Braelon** into **Breece**'s job. Game-by-game they stuck up for **Woody Marks**, framed **Tuten** as a strong RB2 (not RB1), debated whether **Warren** was a missed sell-high, and told 1QB managers to **dump Herbert**. For your rosters: MAIN should be nervous about **Hampton** and curious about **Miller**'s goal-line role; DYNASTY got a spike from **Walker** + **Keenan**, a Dave cold shoulder for **Odunze**, and a reminder that **Braelon**'s production is on a timer once Hall returns.

**Freddy watch:** In DYNASTY, Freddy rostered the show's #1 winner (**Germie Bernard**, Jamey) and Heath's TE winner (**Loveland**). His MAIN QB **Cousins** boomed late (Adam started him in about seven leagues), while **Meyers** (14.3, "better times ahead") and **Henry** (14.8, preferred over Douglas on the wire) scored on his benches. **Kyren Williams**'s "I'm not out there" quote is the one to watch.
